_doc: Pools used to seed Claude with a combinatorial angle. PokerNet AI sells AI bots — fillers (table seeding, off-peak coverage, peak amplification) and regs (configurable +EV play across formats). Revenue-share pricing. Topics MUST stay inside this scope. The 'forbidden_categories' list is hard-fenced — Claude must not draft posts about those topics even if they're poker-adjacent. Anti-repeat log filters exhausted angles.
operator_pains: off-peak desertion — tables empty 02:00-08:00 UTC, rake collapses 60-80% from peak
table seeding — new format/limit tables never reach 4-handed because nobody wants to be the first sitter
peak loading still leaves 30-40% of theoretical seat capacity empty during prime hours
rake-per-table falls when bumhunters arrive — recreational players scatter, table dies in 12 minutes
session-length collapse — players sit, play 5-15 hands, leave; median session falls from 47 to 12 minutes
regulars-only stagnation — field hardens, recreationals stop coming back, rake plateaus
format launch gridlock — operator wants to add PLO5 or Short Deck but cannot get tables started
stake-shopping fragmentation — players split across too many limits, none of them stay alive
high-stakes tables nobody opens despite demand — rake left on the table at 5/10+
tournament late reg drying up — guarantees overlay because nobody late-regs into half-empty fields
competitive pressure — neighbouring club's tables look fuller, players migrate during off-hours
manager attention drain — staff spending hours pinging regulars to seat new tables manually
first-week cohort churn — new player opens lobby, sees 0/6 seated, never deposits again
weekend-vs-weekday rake delta wider than it should be — capacity exists, demand scatters
agent-tier players underperform during off-peak — agents cannot deliver volume promises
expansion to a new platform stalls because seeding from scratch on a fresh club is brutal
operator_solutions_in_scope: fillers seating off-peak tables to keep activity visible to lobby browsers
fillers amplifying peak loading — pushing 4-handed tables to 6-handed, 6-max to fully seated
fillers as table starters — first-mover problem solved, real players join once tables look alive
regs as +EV winrate bots configurable per stake and format
regs balancing field toughness — replacing departed humans without changing field difficulty perceptibly
format-specific bots — PLO bots that play PLO right, Short Deck bots that handle 6+ ranges
low-ban-rate behaviour patterns — natural timing, occasional misclicks, human-like leaks
fast deployment — new client club seeded with bots within days of contract
revenue-share economics — operator pays nothing until rake demonstrably grows
multi-tabling per bot identity — coverage breadth without proportional bot-account overhead
24/7 operational backstop — bots cover hours when manager and agents are asleep
formats: MTT — weekly majors with overlay risk
operator_metrics: rake delta — % uplift before/after bot deployment, typically measured at 30/60/90 days
off-peak loading — % of off-peak seats filled (with vs without fillers)
table-fill-time — minutes from new table open to 4-handed
session-length median — minutes player stays per sit-down
winrate of regs in bb/100 — by stake, by format
ban-rate — bot accounts flagged per 1000 hands played
time-to-launch — days from contract signed to bots seating tables
first-week retention — % of new depositors who return for second session
cohort lifetime rake — average rake-per-player over first 30 days post-first-deposit
field-mix ratio — recreational vs regular density on cash tables
peak-amplification — % seat utilisation at peak with vs without bot top-up
case_study_archetypes: mid-sized 600-player NLH club struggling with 03:00-08:00 desertion — fillers added — rake delta +28% within 60 days
new club launching on PokerBros from zero — full bot seeding from day 1 — first 200 real players onboarded over 6 weeks
established PPPoker club expanding to PLO5 tables — bots provided format starter density — PLO line broke even in 5 weeks
club losing recreationals to neighbouring competitor — regs deployed at lower toughness setting to soften field — recreational retention up 19% over baseline
high-stakes 5/10 NLH never reached critical mass despite demand — fillers at off-peak created perceived activity — real demand consolidated within 4 weeks
tournament series with chronic overlay — late-reg fillers added to keep field looking healthy — overlay reduced 65% across the series
ClubGG club fighting bumhunting — fillers filled the seat after the bumhunter sat to prevent table death — average post-bumhunter session length doubled
differentiators_to_emphasize: revenue-share: clubs pay only when rake grows, no upfront fee, aligned incentives
low ban rate via human-like behaviour patterns (timing variance, natural leaks, occasional misclicks)
format-specific bots — PLO bots aren't NLH bots with different rules, they're trained for the format
fast launch: days from signed contract to deployed bots, not weeks
multi-tabling per identity — operational density without account-farm overhead
configurable winrate for regs — operator controls field toughness, not us
covers all major anonymous-club platforms in one operator relationship
forbidden_categories: payment processing, withdrawal SLA, USDT bridges, payout latency, KYC, AML compliance
licensing, regulation, jurisdictional risk, legal structure
anti-collusion detection or bot-detection methodology as our area of expertise (we make bots, we don't sell detection)
agent hierarchy economics, agent-vs-agent disputes, commission split mechanics
player marketing, traffic acquisition, social media for clubs
VPN setup, hosting infrastructure, hardware farming, account warming logistics
platform rake policy comparison as the main angle (mention rake as context, never as the post topic)
guaranteed rake outcomes — we never write 'guaranteed +25%'; ranges and case data only
named real clubs — every case is anonymized as 'a [size]-player club running [format] on [platform]'
claude_invention_hint: Pool entries are starting points, not a fence. Combine 1 pain + 1 format + 1 platform from the in-scope pools, OR pick a case_study_archetype and dramatize it with realistic numbers. NEVER touch forbidden_categories — if a natural angle would lead there, skip it and pick another. The goal is a post an experienced anonymous-club operator would forward to a colleague: specific to filler/reg use cases, grounded in our actual capability set, with at least one concrete metric or anonymized case detail.
